candidates.name: US-Gas-Prices
candidates.what_it_holds: Python (Selenium) scrapers that pull daily average gas prices from gasprices.aaa.com at state level (scrape_state_daily_averages.py) and metro/457-city level (scrape_metro_daily_averages.py), saving one CSV per day under data/state-daily-averages/ and data/metro-daily-averages/. Repo currently only has one committed snapshot (2026-09-13.csv) at check time -- it is a live/ongoing scrape, not a backfilled history -- but the method is a clean one-command pull of AAA's full state+metro daily average retail gas price panel.
candidates.why_useful: AAA state/metro daily gas price panel is a real-time, high-frequency road-travel cost proxy that speaks to gap #10 (road capacity/traffic) and to consumer discretionary travel spend generally -- higher pump prices are a classic drag on US domestic driving vacations (a chunk of ABNB North America nights). MIT licensed, active as of Sep 2026.
candidates.time_coverage: live-only, started ~Sep 2026 at time of check (grows daily going forward)
candidates.size_hint: 1 CSV/day, ~50 rows (states) or ~457 rows (metros) per file

candidates.name: ScrapeUSGasPrices
candidates.what_it_holds: Python crawler that scrapes daily average gas prices for 457 US cities from the AAA Gas Prices website (gasprices.aaa.com), started ~2019-2022 vintage per repo notes (references a March 2022 outage). Method only in the README snippet seen; check repo tree for any committed historical CSVs.
candidates.why_useful: Another independent AAA city-level gas price scraper, potentially with a longer running history (mentions issues from 2022) than lykmapipo's repo -- worth checking for a multi-year backfill of city-level pump prices.
candidates.time_coverage: unclear from README snippet; scraper referenced issues as far back as March 2022, suggesting it may have run since ~2019-2022
candidates.size_hint: unknown, need to check data/ folder

candidates.name: AAAGas
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper pulling AAA gas prices at metro and state level; metro scrape begins 2024-11-17, state scrape begins the day before (2024-11-16). Includes example plots (Atlanta vs Detroit regular gas). Presumably committed CSVs building daily since Nov 2024, i.e. roughly 2 years of daily state/metro gas price history by the pitch date.
candidates.why_useful: Longest-running AAA scrape found (since Nov 2024) -- if the data files are actually committed and current, this is close to a 2-year daily state+metro gas price panel, useful as a proxy for road-trip cost of US domestic travel and regional consumer strength divergence.
candidates.time_coverage: Nov 2024 - present (~22 months as of Sep 2026)
candidates.size_hint: unknown -- need to check data folder size/row count

candidates.name: AAA-SA-gas-prices
candidates.what_it_holds: Git-scraping style repo (simonw pattern) that scrapes San Antonio, TX average gas prices from AAA's site 4x/day; full history lives in the git commit log of the tracked data file rather than in separate dated files.
candidates.why_useful: Single-city but very high frequency (4x daily) AAA gas price series via git history -- a template for point-in-time gas price vintages if the git log is mined; low standalone value for ABNB (one city) but a useful method example.
candidates.size_hint: single small CSV/JSON, history in git log

candidates.name: eiapy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client wrapping the full EIA Open Data API v2 (222 leaf routes across 13 categories: petroleum, natural gas, electricity, coal, SEDS, STEO, AEO/IEO, etc.), returning typed pandas DataFrames. Petroleum category includes get_data("petroleum","pri","gnd") for retail gasoline/diesel prices (EIA's weekly/monthly regional and national gas price series). Requires a free EIA API key (no payment).
candidates.why_useful: One-command, no-cost, no-scraping pull of EIA's official weekly/monthly retail gasoline and diesel price series (by PADD region and US average), which is the standard non-AAA benchmark for consumer fuel cost and a clean point-in-time-able macro input; also opens EIA's much broader petroleum/energy dataset (jet fuel, refinery data) relevant to travel-cost gap analyses.
candidates.time_coverage: as far back as EIA series go (gasoline weekly since 1990s) via the API
candidates.size_hint: API client, no committed data; pull volume depends on query
candidates.last_activity: recent, under active development per README

candidates.name: oil-prices (Frictionless Data / datasets org)
candidates.what_it_holds: Data package + pipeline script (oil_prices_flow.py, dataflows library) that rebuilds Brent (from 20 May 1987) and WTI Cushing OK (from 2 Jan 1986) spot crude prices at annual/monthly/weekly/daily frequency, sourced from the EIA API. Long-running, well-maintained 'datasets' GitHub org, public domain.
candidates.why_useful: Crude oil price is the upstream driver of retail gasoline/diesel prices and airfare fuel surcharges; a long, clean, well-documented daily/weekly crude series is a useful macro input for a driving-cost or airfare-cost proxy even though it is one step removed from pump prices.
candidates.size_hint: small CSVs, thousands of daily rows over ~39 years
candidates.license: Public domain (US govt data) / PDDL for the wrapper
candidates.last_activity: long-running frictionlessdata/datasets org repo, periodically updated
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: distinct from what we hold (we have FRED CPI/airfares, not this raw Brent/WTI spot series)

candidates.name: nhtsr
candidates.what_it_holds: R package producing eight tidy tibbles (households, persons, vehicles, trips) from the National Household Travel Survey (NHTS) 2017 and 2022 waves, properly typed and labeled from the raw ORNL SPSS files. Lets you compute trip counts, trip length, VMT-adjacent stats by metro size, day of week, etc.
candidates.why_useful: NHTS is the authoritative US household travel behavior survey (trip counts, purpose, length, mode, vehicle ownership) -- useful for road-trip/leisure-travel share of total US travel and for cross-referencing vacation driving behavior against ABNB's North America nights, addressing gap #10 (road travel capacity/behavior) from a demand side rather than price side.
candidates.time_coverage: 2017 and 2022 survey waves (2022 file distributed by ORNL 2022-2024)
candidates.size_hint: microdata, tens of thousands of household/trip records per wave
candidates.license: unspecified in README; underlying NHTS data is public (ORNL/FHWA)
candidates.last_activity: unknown, package supports up to 2022 wave

candidates.name: NHTS2001
candidates.what_it_holds: Compressed 2001 National Household Travel Survey public-use dataset (household/person/vehicle/trip files), packaged for use in the VisionEval travel-demand modeling framework.
candidates.why_useful: Oldest committed NHTS wave found on GitHub (2001) -- useful as a historical baseline for pre-STR-era household travel/driving behavior if a long time-series comparison of road-trip share of travel is ever built.
candidates.size_hint: compressed microdata files, national household survey scale (tens of thousands of records)

candidates.name: world-infrastructure-data-hub
candidates.what_it_holds: Daily-refreshed, GitHub-Actions-built static JSON API (countries.json, per-country files) covering retail gasoline/diesel/LPG prices (USD/L) for ~130 countries from the EU Weekly Oil Bulletin and World Bank Global Fuel Prices DB, plus household electricity price, CO2/capita, and 8 World Bank socioeconomic indicators (GDP/capita, inflation, unemployment, Gini, etc.) for 167-170 countries. Live endpoint: https://aykutsp.github.io/world-infrastructure-data-hub/api/v1/countries.json. v1.1 adds 15-year historical time series with sparklines for CO2 and World Bank indicators.
candidates.why_useful: A global (not just US) retail gasoline price panel by country is directly relevant to ABNB's EMEA/LatAm/APAC regional consumer-fuel-cost proxies and could feed a cross-region driving-cost index alongside FX and inflation, touching both gap #7 (regional travel volume/consumer strength) and the road-travel theme; free, no-key, machine-readable JSON API refreshed daily.
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot daily; v1.1 adds historical time series (up to 15 years) for CO2/World Bank fields (fuel price history not stated as historized)
candidates.license: MIT (code) / CC BY 4.0 and ODbL for underlying data sources

candidates.name: fuelfeed
candidates.what_it_holds: Cloudflare-Workers-based real-time UK fuel price aggregator pulling from 15+ UK retailers (ASDA, BP, Esso, Shell, Tesco, Morrisons, Sainsbury's, Jet, Gulf, Texaco, etc.) via the UK government's official Fuel Finder API/CSV feed, updated hourly to real-time, exposed as a public JSON/GeoJSON API (/api/data.json, /api/data.mapbox). mirror.mjs script performs the data mirroring.
candidates.why_useful: UK retail fuel price panel at station level, sourced from the UK govt Fuel Finder scheme -- relevant to EMEA regional driving-cost/consumer-strength proxy (a UK-specific complement to the aykutsp global country-level series), and demonstrates a clean method for turning a public government feed into a queryable API.
candidates.time_coverage: live/real-time only, no historical archive apparent

candidates.name: bureau-of-transportation-statistics (API Evangelist profile)
candidates.what_it_holds: Third-party API profile (apis.yml/apis.json plus Postman/OpenAPI collections) pointing to the US Bureau of Transportation Statistics's public API surface: the BTS Open Data Socrata (SODA) portal (data.bts.gov), TranStats (airline on-time performance, carrier/airport snapshots, fuel consumption -- this is BTS T-100/DB1B territory, already a named gap #10 target), and the Freight Analysis Framework (FAF) for domestic/international freight flow volume and value by mode.
candidates.why_useful: Not itself a road/fuel dataset, but a ready-made, machine-readable index (Postman + OpenAPI collections) of every BTS API surface -- aviation (T-100/DB1B), freight (FAF), and general transportation economics -- directly matching gap #10's 'BTS T-100/DB1B' and freight/road capacity ask, and could shortcut discovery of a BTS 'Highway Statistics'/VMT-adjacent Socrata dataset via data.bts.gov.
candidates.time_coverage: n/a (API index, not a data snapshot)
candidates.license: unclear for the profile repo itself (informational); underlying BTS data is public govt data

candidates.name: fuel-price-finder
candidates.what_it_holds: Real-time fuel price and EV charging finder app; README notes prices update daily ("not real-time"), CSV reflects prices reported by 08:00, not all independent stations report. Appears to be a build tutorial/app rather than a data archive; geography and source unclear from snippet (needs verification of underlying feed, likely US or UK government open fuel-price feed).
candidates.why_useful: Possible additional method for pulling a daily station-level fuel price CSV feed; lower confidence than fuelfeed/AAA repos above since geography/source were not confirmed by full README read.

notes: This session's WebSearch tool budget was exhausted before I could run any query with it (0 usable calls) -- likely drained by other concurrent scout sessions sharing the same session-level quota. I substituted Google/DuckDuckGo/Bing fetched via WebFetch (mostly blocked by 403/429 on direct fetch of search-engine result pages) and then switched to the claude-in-chrome browser tool driving real Google searches, which worked well and is what produced all the candidates above. Future scouts hitting the same WebSearch exhaustion should go straight to the browser-driven Google search path rather than iterating on WebFetch against search engines (Google blocks WebFetch's UA/renders JS-light snippets acceptably; DuckDuckGo html/lite endpoints return 403 to WebFetch; Bing's page renders but the small extraction model summarizes away URLs). Dead ends: toll/turnpike/EZPass, holiday-travel-forecast, and diesel-trucking-index searches returned almost nothing on-topic -- toll data and AAA holiday-travel-volume projections do not appear to have any GitHub presence (the AAA holiday travel forecast numbers themselves are only published as PDF/press releases, not committed as data anywhere found). The strongest single find is jgreathouse9/AAAGas (state+metro AAA gas prices since Nov 2024, ~22 months of daily data) if its data folder is confirmed populated -- worth a follow-up repo-tree check before relying on it. eiapy is the cleanest no-scrape path to EIA's official weekly gasoline/diesel price series by PADD region. NHTS packages (nhtsr, NHTS2001) are travel-behavior surveys rather than road/fuel data per se but were flagged since they bear on gap #10's broader 'road capacity and traffic' ask and cross-reference with the party-size/travel-behavior gap (#20).
